candidate.title: PRO-seq
candidate.scope: Assigned single, ungrouped PRO-seq poster row: the middle horizontal route labeled PRO-seq, from engaged Pol II/nascent RNA through four separately processed single-biotin-NTP reactions to cDNA for each nucleotide. The supplied card identifies source_method_labels=[PRO-seq] and grouped_source_row=false. The independently labeled 4sUDRB-seq and PRO-cap rows have no alternative-workflow or material-transfer arrows connecting them to PRO-seq; they are visible context, as are clipped upper-border content and the EDTA structure beyond the right panel boundary. This revision removes the previously over-included neighboring routes and their unrelated Unknowns while preserving all four PRO-seq reaction histories. Scope is the depicted four-reaction implementation clarified by Kwak et al. (2013), not every implementation in the broader PRO-seq family. Extraction ends at the cDNA products; 3′-end sequencing is explained as readout interpretation without adding unshown sequencing, alignment or pooling operations.

operations.description: PRO-seq A-only branch: engaged Pol II incorporates the supplied biotin-A nucleotide into nascent RNA, creating a labeled RNA end close to its pre-run-on polymerase position.

method_scopes.rationale: The middle row and matching collection page describe four separate reactions, each receiving one biotin-NTP type, ending in cDNA for each nucleotide. Every local preparation step is therefore instantiated separately for A, C, G and U, without an invented pooling or integration step. One type per reaction does not mean exactly one incorporation per molecule: Kwak reports one or at most a few identical bases. The readout is the nascent-RNA 3′ end near run-on-competent Pol II, copied into cDNA; arrested/backtracked complexes are a catalogue-reported limitation. No DRB or cap-selective preparation is assigned to this row. The assigned card is explicitly ungrouped; therefore the neighboring 4sUDRB-seq and PRO-cap rows, including the latter’s mention in Kwak, are excluded from this record. This repairs the scope finding without removing or merging any in-scope nucleotide branch.
